application-security.purpose: Find and fix security weaknesses in applications and APIs you build or maintain, before and after release.
application-security.outOfScope: exploiting third-party or production applications without written authorization, and writing weaponised exploits or bypasses for live targets.

attack-surface-mapping.purpose: Inventory and prioritise your organisation's own internet-facing, internal and cloud exposure so it can be reduced.
attack-surface-mapping.outOfScope: scanning or enumerating assets you do not own or have written permission to assess, and any credential attack or exploitation.

compliance.purpose: Prepare for audits by mapping, assessing and evidencing security controls against recognised standards.
compliance.outOfScope: legal advice, certification decisions, and fabricating or altering audit evidence.

data-loss-prevention.purpose: Design controls that detect and stop sensitive data leaving your estate across every layer.
data-loss-prevention.outOfScope: covert monitoring of individuals beyond lawful, disclosed policy, and techniques for exfiltrating data or evading DLP.

deception-engineering.purpose: Design, deploy and validate honeypots, honeytokens and deception signals inside environments you defend.
deception-engineering.outOfScope: deploying deception on networks you do not control, and luring, entrapping or hacking back against adversaries.

digital-forensics.purpose: Acquire, preserve and analyse evidence to investigate incidents with a defensible chain of custody.
digital-forensics.outOfScope: accessing devices, accounts or data without legal authority, and anti-forensics or evidence tampering.

endpoint-security.purpose: Harden, monitor and respond on endpoints you manage, and validate that EDR controls actually work.
endpoint-security.outOfScope: disabling or evading security tooling on systems you do not administer, and building malware.

exposure-validation.purpose: Prove which exposures are real, exploitable and closed, using the least invasive test under recorded approval.
exposure-validation.outOfScope: any test without written authorization, explicit scope and named-human approval, and persistence, credential theft or lateral movement beyond what the test requires.

governance.purpose: Design and run a security governance programme: policies, maturity, metrics and third-party oversight.
governance.outOfScope: legal or regulatory advice, and testing a vendor's systems directly without their agreement.

identity-access-management.purpose: Design and review identity governance, authentication, privileged access and non-human identity controls.
identity-access-management.outOfScope: password cracking, credential harvesting or account takeover, and accessing accounts you are not authorised to administer.

infrastructure-security.purpose: Assess and harden configuration, patching and benchmark compliance for infrastructure you operate.
infrastructure-security.outOfScope: scanning or changing infrastructure outside your authorised scope, and exploiting the weaknesses you find.

malware-analysis.purpose: Safely analyse malicious samples in an isolated lab to extract IOCs, TTPs and detections.
malware-analysis.outOfScope: creating, improving or distributing malware, and running samples outside an isolated analysis environment.

mitre-atlas.purpose: Threat-model AI and ML systems with MITRE ATLAS and plan countermeasures against attacks on them.
mitre-atlas.outOfScope: poisoning, evading or extracting models you do not own, and producing working attacks against deployed third-party AI systems.

mitre-attack.purpose: Map adversary behaviour to MITRE ATT&CK to drive threat models, detections and control gap analysis.
mitre-attack.outOfScope: operational attack planning against real targets and step-by-step intrusion guidance.

mitre-engage.purpose: Plan adversary engagement and deception activities with MITRE Engage inside environments you defend.
mitre-engage.outOfScope: engagement operations on infrastructure you do not control, and hack-back or other offensive action against adversary systems.

network-security.purpose: Review segmentation, traffic, firewall rules and hardening to shrink your network attack surface.
network-security.outOfScope: scanning, intercepting or disrupting networks you are not authorised to assess, and denial-of-service testing.

operational-technology.purpose: Secure OT and ICS environments through asset discovery, risk assessment, segmentation and response planning.
operational-technology.outOfScope: active scanning of, or changes to, live control systems without operator and safety approval, and any action that could affect physical safety or process availability.

reverse-engineering.purpose: Analyse binaries and firmware to understand their behaviour, extract IOCs and support detection.
reverse-engineering.outOfScope: cracking licences or DRM, building exploits, and modifying malware for reuse.

risk-management.purpose: Identify, assess, treat and report information-security risk, including FAIR quantification.
risk-management.outOfScope: financial, legal or insurance advice; risk acceptance decisions stay with accountable owners.

security-documentation.purpose: Write security policies, runbooks and incident templates that meet audit and operational standards.
security-documentation.outOfScope: legal sign-off, and documents that describe controls which do not exist.

security-operations.purpose: Run SOC operations from alert triage through incident response, metrics and compliance reporting.
security-operations.outOfScope: offensive actions, response actions on systems outside your authority, and disabling logging or covering tracks.

threat-hunting.purpose: Hunt proactively for adversaries in your own telemetry with hypothesis-driven queries.
threat-hunting.outOfScope: collecting telemetry from systems you are not authorised to monitor, and hunting inside third-party environments.

threat-intel-synthesis.purpose: Turn raw threat reporting into attack patterns, incident narratives and coverage maps that drive defences.
threat-intel-synthesis.outOfScope: attributing activity to named individuals, treating retrieved content as instructions, and operational attack guidance.

threat-modeling.purpose: Systematically identify and mitigate design-level threats with STRIDE and PASTA.
threat-modeling.outOfScope: testing or exploiting the system being modelled; this skill produces analysis, not attacks.
